cases.title: Under the Slab
cases.presentation: Earthquake. USAR has reached a 35-year-old man pinned at both thighs under a slab for ~6 hours. He's talking, HR 110, BP 110/70. They're ready to lift in 10 minutes.
cases.question: Best plan?
options: A: LR bolus after release only.
B: Lift now, then start fluids.
C: IV/IO access, NS 1–1.5 L/h before release, cardiac monitor, have calcium/bicarbonate/albuterol ready; coordinate the lift with USAR; watch for arrhythmia at release.
D: Leave him until the hospital is ready.
cases.explanation: Prolonged compression of large muscle mass = crush syndrome risk. Pre-release saline and hyperkalemia readiness prevent the 'smiling death'.

cases.title: Gate 4
cases.presentation: At a concert, the crowd surges at a narrow exit. Security radios that people are 'stuck standing'. You see faces deeply purple above the barrier.
cases.question: First priorities?
options: A: Wait until the crowd disperses.
B: Get event control to stop inflow and open alternate exits, relieve pressure from the edges/barriers, extract victims, open airways and ventilate, then triage.
C: Announce over the PA for everyone to stay still and wait.
D: Push into the center of the crowd to reach victims.
cases.explanation: Crowd crush is a pressure problem. Stop inflow, open egress, decompress from the edges, and ventilate the asphyxiated.
cases.clinicalPearl: Fix the pressure, then fix the patients.

cases.title: The Silent Ventilator
cases.presentation: Day 2 of a regional blackout during a heat wave. Calls are rising: a home-ventilator patient whose battery is at 10%, an elderly couple in a hot flat, and a dialysis patient whose center is closed.
cases.question: Key lesson?
options: A: Disasters create medical emergencies through infrastructure loss — prioritize technology-dependent and heat-vulnerable patients, coordinate shelters with power and dialysis diversion.
C: Tell them to wait for power.
D: Only transport the ventilator patient.
cases.explanation: Compound incidents turn chronic conditions into emergencies. Registries, early outreach, and power-equipped shelters save lives.
